content: # Prove square-root lower bound for LP-compatible policies in degenerate restless bandits This file contains the open problem on Prove square-root lower bound for LP-compatible policies in degenerate restless bandits. --- ## 1. Prove square-root lower bound for LP-compatible policies in degenerate restless bandits Source paper authors: Nicolas Gast, Bruno Gaujal, Chen Yan ### 1. Problem Background Consider a discrete-time finite-horizon restless bandit with a population of $N$ statistically identical arms. Each arm has a finite state space $S=\{1,\dots,d\}$ and two actions $a\in\{0,1\}$ (passive/active). If an arm is in state $s$ and action $a$ is chosen, an immediate reward $R_s^a\in\mathbb{R}$ is earned and the arm transitions to state $s'$ with probability $P^{a}_{s,s'}$. Arms evolve independently conditional on actions. At each time $t=0,1,\dots,T-1$, exactly a fraction $\alpha\in(0,1)$ of arms is activated (with the convention that if $\alpha N$ is not an integer, the policy randomizes between $\lfloor \alpha N\rfloor$ and $\lfloor \alpha N\rfloor+1$ active arms so that the expected number of active arms equals $\alpha N$). Let $M^{(N)}(t)\in\Delta_d$ be the empirical distribution of arm states at time $t$, where $M^{(N)}_s(t)$ is the fraction of arms in state $s$. Let $Y^{(N)}(t)\in\Delta_{2d}$ be the empirical state-action fractions, where $Y^{(N)}_{s,a}(t)$ is the fraction of arms in state $s$ assigned action $a$ at time $t$. The per-arm reward of a policy $\pi$ is $$ V^{(N)}_{\pi}(m(0),T):=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\Big[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}} R_s^a\,Y^{(N)}_{s,a}(t)\Big]. $$ The standard LP relaxation replaces the hard per-time activation constraint by an equality constraint on expected activation. Writing $y_{s,a}(t):=\mathbb{E}[Y^{(N)}_{s,a}(t)]$, the relaxation value $V_{\mathrm{rel}}(m(0),T)$ is the optimum of $$ \max_{y\ge 0}\ \sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\sum_{s,a} R_s^a\,y_{s,a}(t) $$ subject to flow conservation $$ y_{s,0}(t+1)+y_{s,1}(t+1)=\sum_{s'\in S}\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}} y_{s',a}(t)P^{a}_{s',s}\quad \forall s,\ t, $$ activation budget $$ \sum_{s\in S} y_{s,1}(t)=\alpha\quad\forall t, $$ and initial condition $y_{s,0}(0)+y_{s,1}(0)=m_s(0)$. Call a Markovian admissible policy $\pi=\{\pi_t\}_{t=0}^{T-1}$ a map $\pi_t:\Delta_d\to\Delta_{2d}$ that, given state distribution $m$, prescribes fractions $y=\pi_t(m)$ satisfying $y_{s,a}\ge 0$, $\sum_a y_{s,a}=m_s$ for all $s$, and $\sum_s y_{s,1}=\alpha$. A policy is LP-compatible if there exists an optimal LP solution $\{y^*(t)\}_{t=0}^{T-1}$ such that $\pi_t(m^*(t))=y^*(t)$ for all $t$, where $m^*_s(t)=y^*_{s,0}(t)+y^*_{s,1}(t)$. Let $S_0(t):=\{s\in S: y^*_{s,0}(t)>0\text{ and } y^*_{s,1}(t)>0\}$. The model is called degenerate if for every optimal LP solution there exists at least one time $t$ such that $|S_0(t)|=0$, i.e., at that time the LP solution activates some states fully and leaves the rest fully passive with no state partially split between actions. The paper provides an example showing that for some degenerate models, the LP-relaxation gap under any LP-compatible policy cannot decay faster than order $1/\sqrt{N}$, and formulates a general conjecture that this phenomenon is typical for degenerate models. ### 2. Open Problem **Question 1.1.** For a fixed finite-horizon restless bandit instance $(S,\{P^a\}_{a\in\{0,1\}},\{R^a\}_{a\in\{0,1\}},\alpha,T,m(0))$ that is degenerate in the sense that for some time $t$ every optimal solution $\{y^*(\tau)\}_{\tau=0}^{T-1}$ of the LP relaxation satisfies $|S_0(t)|=0$, determine whether the following statement holds (as conjectured in the paper): There exist constants $\underline C,\overline C>0$ (depending on the instance but not on $N$) such that for every LP-compatible admissible policy $\pi$ and all sufficiently large $N$, $$ \frac{\underline C}{\sqrt{N}}\ \le\ \bigl|V^{(N)}_{\pi}(m(0),T)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(m(0),T)\bigr|\ \le\ \frac{\overline C}{\sqrt{N}}. $$ In particular, the task is to prove or disprove the $\Omega(1/\sqrt{N})$ lower bound on the LP-relaxation optimality gap for LP-compatible policies on (essentially all) degenerate finite-horizon restless bandits. ### 3. Known Results In Gast--Gaujal--Yan (2023), finite-horizon homogeneous restless bandits are analyzed via the relaxed LP (flow constraints plus per-time expected activation). A key dichotomy is between non-degenerate instances (every optimal LP solution has at least one split state at every time) where locally linear LP-compatible policies exist and yield exponentially small gaps to $V_{\mathrm{rel}}$, and degenerate instances (some time $t$ has $|S_0(t)|=0$) where the paper gives a concrete example with an unavoidable $\Theta(1/\sqrt N)$ gap for LP-compatible policies and conjectures this is typical. The open problem asks to prove a universal $\Omega(1/\sqrt N)$ lower bound (and matching $O(1/\sqrt N)$ upper bound) for the LP-relaxation gap of any LP-compatible policy on essentially all degenerate finite-horizon instances. Forward citations provide partial evidence but no general resolution. The strongest supporting result is the Gaussian-approximation line of work ("Achieving O (1/N) optimality gap in restless bandits through Gaussian approximation" / "Achieving Optimality Gap in Restless Bandits through Gaussian Approximation"), which proves that for a specific degenerate example, every policy in a broad fluid/LP-tracking class has $\Theta(1/\sqrt N)$ optimality gap and that the LP upper bound itself can be $\Theta(1/\sqrt N)$ above the true $N$-arm optimum. This bolsters the view that when the optimal LP trajectory lies on a boundary (as in $|S_0(t)|=0$), CLT-scale fluctuations in the empirical state can force a square-root loss for policies that track the LP prescription. At the same time, that work also shows that second-order (Gaussian/stochastic-programming) policies can achieve $\tilde O(1/N)$ gaps to the true optimum under a uniqueness condition, indicating that the $1/\sqrt N$ obstruction is tied to LP/fluid compatibility rather than to the RMAB itself. Other forward citations mainly develop complementary upper-bound theories in infinite-horizon average-reward settings (e.g., MPC/LP-update policies with $O(1/\sqrt N)$ gaps under mixing and exponential gaps under nondegeneracy/stability; focus-set/ID policies with $O(1/\sqrt N)$ gaps under unichain/aperiodicity), and general convex-optimization sensitivity tools that explain why degeneracy blocks second-order improvements. A few works on weakly coupled multi-action systems claim exponential convergence to relaxed LP values without nondegeneracy under Lipschitz-type conditions, but these conditions plausibly exclude the discontinuities inherent in the degenerate $|S_0(t)|=0$ regime. Overall, the conjectured universal $\Omega(1/\sqrt N)$ lower bound for all LP-compatible policies across essentially all degenerate finite-horizon instances remains open; existing results establish $\Theta(1/\sqrt N)$ lower bounds for substantial LP/fluid-tracking policy classes on explicit degenerate examples and suggest that proving universality will require a general argument linking boundary optimal LP solutions to unavoidable CLT-scale rounding/mismatch losses. #### 3.1 Upstream solution and partial-progress records - [Partial progress #101 (PDF)](https://pranav-nuti.github.io/open-problems-in-or/data/llm_math_export/solution_progress/W4389224581_p0/partial_progress/101.pdf) - [pipeline final 101](https://pranav-nuti.github.io/open-problems-in-or/data/llm_math_export/solution_progress/W4389224581_p0/partial_progress/pipeline_final_101.pdf) ### 4.
